Console pulse — pocket log

TL;DR: quick brain dump while triaging console/dash reports. Short checklist + playbook snippets I can reuse. Not polished — notes to self and next actions.

2026-03-13 09:12 — startup
- Warmed up: checked main console landing dashboard, 95th token-latency spiked around 08:45 UTC for hosted-api-prod route.
- Customer ticket INF-2893: user reports streaming drops (partial chunks, reconnects). Severity: P2 (sporadic, multiple orgs).

Immediate quick checks (what I run first)
- query: last 6h latency heatmap (route=hosted-api-prod) -> look for convoys at 08:30-09:00
- logs: grep streaming errors: "stream closed by client" vs "broken pipe"
- infra: check dedicated pool utilization for same timeframe (GPU saturations?)
- fallback: confirm if automatic fallback to small-variant model kicked in (should be logged in routing trace)

Repro steps (from support + my quick probe)
1) Start a stream on hosted-api-prod (dev token) using a ~1k token prompt
2) Observe chunk arrival times in browser devtools + X-Request-ID
3) Correlate X-Request-ID with trace id in console -> check route decisions and fallback events

Hypotheses (ranked)
- H1: Transient network flakiness between frontend LB and inference nodes -> manifests as chunk drops but request completes after reconnect.
- H2: Routing policy toggled to larger models under load -> increased CPU/GPU queue causing chunk pacing; streaming encoder buffer underflow.
- H3: Client-side backpressure + connection timeout mismatch (older SDK clients)

Quick mitigation steps I attempted
- Restarted small number of routers in us-west-2 staging mimic (no direct effect in prod).
- Applied a soft throttle rule to reduce max chunk size on a canary route (observing).

What to tell support (one-liner to paste)
- "Thanks — investigating streaming spikes. I've correlated your X-Request-IDs to routing traces; working hypothesis is transient routing/backpressure. Will follow up with root cause and ETA for a fix within 24h."

Owner/next actions
- Ethan: collect 1h of aligned traces + attach to INF-2893 (by 13:00 PST)
- Riley: check dedicated pool metrics + GPU queue lengths (by EOD)
- Asha: push lightweight SDK compatibility note to #console-notices (optional)

Follow-ups / reminders
- Remind infra to add an explicit log field for "stream-chunk-drop" (ticket INF-2912)
- Add a small dashboard card: "stream chunk rate / minute" (low cardinality)
- Schedule 30m sync with product-owner if recurring (if >3 incidents in 72h)

Playbook snippet: triage ladder (quick reference)
1) Determine scope: single user vs org vs global (use sample rate + user-id counts)
2) Severity decision: when >1% of requests impacted or multiple customers -> P1/P2 escalation
3) Quick mitigations: route throttle, fallback to cached model variant, increase client keepalive if safe
4) Capture data: traces, X-Request-IDs, sampling of raw stream frames
5) Post-incident: add regression alert (eval set + golden prompt)

Useful queries/commands (copyable)
- Grafana: dashboard?panelId=streaming-latency&orgId=1&from=-6h
- Kibana: logs query -> status:500 OR message:/stream.*closed/ AND route:hosted-api-prod
- k8s: kubectl logs -n console router-xyz --since=2h | grep "fallback"

Notes to self (random)
- SDK v0.9.4 had a keepalive bug; check if customer uses it.
- If fallback is observed frequently, ensure rollback window for canary is automatic in console rollouts.
- Consider a short-term feature flag to increase client-side reconnect tolerance for streaming consumers.

Open questions
- Did any recent rollout touch the streaming encoder? (check PRs + changelog)
- Are there correlated infra maintenance events at 08:40 UTC yesterday? (pagerduty logs)

Wrap-up line: keep this as ephemeral pocket reference — once we resolve INF-2893, move distilled notes to the support ticket and create a short postmortem bullet list in shared_drives/customer-success/ (if we need to notify more customers).
